task: Interpretation of one already-admitted managed peer-review job; no new job was started and none was restarted.
statusSource: No live status call was made. This session exposes no status interface for the specialist that ran this job. What is recorded below comes from the preserved job record, and it was checked against the files on disk by recomputing the SHA-256 and byte count of every declared artifact.

contentObservations.detail: Recommendation is major revision, with 1 issue classified fatal, 4 major and 18 minor (23 checked).

The rubric layer settled on a universal rubric plus the PRISMA 2020 checklist, 21 and 27 items respectively, and refused three instruments as inappropriate: the scoping-review extension, the randomised-trial reporting standard and a narrative-review exemption. Each refusal gives the same reason, that the submission is a systematic review of trials and not a single trial, a scoping review or a narrative review.

contentObservations.observation: Verbatim-quote layer is genuinely degraded, and the review says so
contentObservations.detail: 13 quotes were checked against the parsed text and 5 were located. 8 could not be found and 4 findings were demoted as a result, while a further 11 carry no quote at all. Reviewers should read those 4 items at lower confidence than the rest; the demotion is disclosed in the run record and was not quietly absorbed.

contentObservations.observation: What the review in fact critiques
contentObservations.detail: The critical items target how complete and legible the submitted text is, with repeated and concatenated headings and broken section bodies, an unbalanced discussion with no implementation-limits section, and claims of 'no systematic difference' between older and newer trials that rest on subjective judgement with no reported test statistic, test method or interval.
contentObservations.source: peer-review-report.md critical issues and the rubric table

contentObservations.observation: Reported statistics are not re-computed by this engine
contentObservations.detail: A statistical recomputation module is recorded as skipped, on the stated reason that the engine does not recompute reported statistics. Whether the manuscript's pooled result agrees numerically with its underlying data therefore falls outside what this job checked.

Coverage of the rule sets was reported as partial for the parsed document, and the review treats unparsed or unreadable regions as not assessable instead of absent. The fatal item is framed as a text-integrity problem and keeps an explicit alternative open, that the defect may come from extraction rather than from the submission.

contentObservations.observation: Applicability of the checklist applied, item by item
contentObservations.detail: Both rule sets were scored item by item, and the tallies differ sharply. The systematic-review reporting checklist, 27 items, yields 1 pass, 3 partial, 8 uncertain and 15 fail, so its failures cluster in how the search, the risk-of-bias handling, the synthesis and the certainty were reported; rationale and objectives hold up. The universal rubric, 21 items, yields 2 pass, 11 partial, 6 uncertain and 2 fail. What it flags is mostly partial compliance instead of missing material.
contentObservations.source: peer-review-report.md item-level tables, counted directly from the report's own verdict column

limitationsVisibleInOutput: No live status query was possible in this session. Terminal state and integrity come from the preserved job record and from recomputing the file hashes locally.
The review rests on a fallback text extraction, because the preferred PDF parser was unavailable in that run. Quote-level findings are therefore sensitive to parse quality.
8 of the 13 candidate quotes could not be located and 11 findings carry no quote. 4 findings were demoted accordingly.
The engine does not recompute reported statistics, so it can neither confirm nor refute the manuscript's pooled numbers.
Handling of the same-trial/submission relationship is limited to what the job recorded as superseded-instrument protection; no independent check of that bond was possible here.
The workspace copy of the manuscript was hashed, but nothing beyond its name and size ties it to the file that was reviewed.
